item.title: Doubly Intermittent Singular Skew Products
item.description: arXiv:2611.31490v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a large class of skew product systems, which can also be thought of as random dynamical systems, coupling a uniformly expanding circle map with a full branch interval map with two indifferent fixed points and unbounded derivatives. This significantly generalizes the setting of several skew products considered in the literature, in particular the Gou\"ezel skew products [Gou\"ezel, Statistical properties of a skew product with a curve of neutral points, Erg. Th. & Dyn. Sys. (2007)], in which the fibre maps are intermittency maps with a single indifferent fixed point and bounded derivatives. Through the construction of an induced full branch map, we prove various statistical properties of the skew products, including existence of an invariant probability measure equivalent to Lebesgue and decay of correlations.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Luzzatto, Rizwan Rizwanullah

item.title: Realization of expanding dynamics by a finite horizon parabolic law response
item.description: arXiv:2611.31618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the discrete dynamical system generated by iterating an episodic response of a population density. In each episode, the running potential is frozen at the current density, agents solve a quadratic control problem, and the terminal density is passed to the next episode. For each prescribed positive horizon $\tau$ and each $C^k$ map $F$ of finitely many Fourier moments, with $1\le k<\infty$, we construct a finite mode interaction realizing $F$ at order $\varepsilon$. In scaled coordinates, the exact parabolic response satisfies $\|T^{(d)}_{\varepsilon,\tau}-(F,S(\tau)|_{\Es_d})\|_{C^k}\le C\varepsilon$. The estimate is uniform over a full bounded infinite dimensional Sobolev fibre and needs neither Fourier truncation nor an invariant manifold. For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches that strictly cover their convex hull, this $C^1$ control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets of the exact response. These sets factor onto the full one sided shift and contain periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue, and hyperbolicity requires a separate strict multiplier condition. We also prove a derivative cost obstruction for nonaffine microscopic realization, a susceptibility weighted criterion for population energy designs, and the failure of exact scalar closure under nontrivial rank one feedback. The results concern designed frozen law responses, not Nash consistent mean field game equilibria or finite player limits.
item.dc:creator: Masood Shahbaz Shoukat, Luca Di Persio, Wensheng Jia

item.title: Spatial switching near a four-loop homoclinic bouquet: a mechanism for multi-bump bound states in coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.31846v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how a localized standing wave of a coupled nonlinear Schr\"odinger (CNLS) system can switch between components from one pulse to the next. The standing wave reduction of the CNLS system yields a four-dimensional Hamiltonian system with two reflection symmetries, in which four elementary pulses correspond to a bouquet of homoclinic loops to a saddle. For saddle eigenvalues $\pm\lambda_{1},\pm\lambda_{2}$ satisfying $0<\lambda_{1} < \lambda_{2} < 2\lambda_1$, and under suitable nondegeneracy assumptions, we construct stable and unstable invariant manifolds of the four-loop bouquet. Apart from trajectories asymptotic to the saddle in the corresponding time direction, these manifolds characterize one-sided trapping near the bouquet within the critical Hamiltonian level, namely the level set containing the saddle equilibrium. Both manifolds have codimension one in this level. We prove that if they intersect transversely away from the bouquet, producing super-homoclinic orbits, then there exist infinitely many multi-bump homoclinic orbits to the saddle. These orbits correspond to multi-bump localized standing waves of the CNLS system.
item.dc:creator: Sajjad Bakrani

item.title: Linearization for unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth
item.description: arXiv:2611.31911v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate global topological linearization with unbounded perturbations of sublinear growth. Under a spectral gap condition and a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, we show that the displacements of both the conjugacy and its inverse from the identity satisfy the same growth bound as the perturbation. Moreover, the conjugacy is unique within the class of maps whose displacements satisfy this bound. We obtain representations of the displacement in terms of stable and unstable orbit series that converge uniformly on any bounded set and give the inverse conjugacy by using the Banach fixed points theorem in a weighted function space.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Tang, Jiangqiong Yu

item.title: Saddle-focus to saddle transition of 4D heteroclinic orbits resembling oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some dissipative Boussinesq systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.31934v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation. The associated traveling wave equations are solutions of four-dimensional dynamical systems, leading to both computational challenges and rich structural behavior. In particular, to describe the properties of these traveling waves, we analyze heteroclinic orbits that connect two distinct equilibria, one of which undergoes a transition in the four-dimensional phase space from a saddle-focus to a saddle point as the dissipation parameter increases. This transition governs the nature of the wave profile, which evolves smoothly from an oscillatory shock wave to a regularized (non-oscillatory) shock wave. To compute such solutions, we introduce a finite-difference-based numerical method tailored for this class of problems.
item.dc:creator: Rezwana Razzaque Angana, Brendan Harding, Dimitrios Mitsotakis

item.title: Dissipative Geometric Flows and Certified Phase-Volume Contraction
item.description: arXiv:2611.32079v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops an approach to uniform phase-volume contraction for prescribed dynamical systems. The main result is that every positive rate strictly below the invariant-measure bound can be certified in finite search time by a regularized Sobolev gradient flow. The resulting positive density ensures exponential contraction of the weighted phase volume with unit prefactor. For each fixed regularization parameter, the flow converges exponentially to a unique minimizer. As the regularization vanishes, these minimizers converge to the feasible potential of minimum Sobolev norm for a fixed feasibility margin. The certification procedure rests on a Holder estimate that converts a bound on the integral penalty into a pointwise bound on the weighted divergence over the entire invariant domain. This estimate yields a stopping criterion for the search. Finite termination is also established in growing finite-dimensional trial spaces for a staged scheme with exact gradient evaluations and controlled positive quadrature. The scheme requires neither a supplied feasibility margin nor a bound on the norm of a feasible potential. A disk example shows that the invariant-measure bound can be approached by smooth certificates even when no C^1 certificate attains it. Analytical properties of novel local D-Liouville, D-Yamabe, and D-Ricci evolutions driven by divergence penalties are established. For the unnormalized D-Yamabe flow, a scaling obstruction to exponential stability of stationary conformal factors is established. For the D-Ricci flow, the transformation law for the prescribed vector field under DeTurck pullback is derived. This law specifies how the vector field must transform when the gauge term is removed. Examples on the torus and sphere identify obstructions to smooth convergence of the geometric evolutions.
item.dc:creator: Igor Furtat

item.title: Twisted Poincar\'e series at zero on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.32648v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(\Sigma,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, Riemannian Anosov surface. We show that there exists an open subset $\mathcal V_g$ of the space of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the fundamental group of $\Sigma$, whose complement has complex codimension at least one, such that the following holds: for all $x,y\in \Sigma$, $\rho \in \mathcal{V}_g$, the meromorphic extension of the twisted Poincar\'e series $s \mapsto \eta_{g,\rho,x,y}(s)$ vanishes at $s=0$. We also give examples of non-trivial representations whose Poincar\'e series does not vanish at zero. In addition, we describe the structure of twisted resonant states at zero for these examples and show that they admit non-trivial Jordan blocks.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Humbert, Thibault Lefeuvre, Sebasti\'an Mu\~noz-Thon, Zhongkai Tao

item.title: Counting periodic points of rational self-maps of projective varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.32875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the number of isolated periodic points of a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety. We first give an upper bound for this number in terms of the degrees of the iterates of the map, thereby extending a theorem of Dinh--Nguyen--Truong to arbitrary characteristic. Our approach is purely algebraic and bypasses the theory of densities of positive closed currents. We then establish the exact asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points of birational self-maps of surfaces over a field of characteristic 0. To do so, we extend Jonsson--Reschke's argument to any finitely generated field over $ \mathbb Q $ using Moriwaki's theory of heights.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Li

item.title: Elimination Methods for Computing Invariant Algebraic Surfaces and Hopf Bifurcations
item.description: arXiv:2611.32912v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents efficient algorithmic methods for computing invariant algebraic surfaces and Hopf bifurcations in parametric polynomial differential systems. For invariant algebraic surfaces of bounded degree, we establish two complementary elimination frameworks: combining Gr\"obner bases with saturation and prime decomposition yields the Zariski closure of the parameter existence locus (necessary conditions), whereas triangular decomposition into strong regular systems recovers the exact pointwise constructible locus (necessary and sufficient conditions) via the projection property. We further present a hybrid approach for identifying such surfaces by integrating prime decomposition with branch-wise triangular solving, thereby efficiently deriving necessary and sufficient conditions with enhanced computational flexibility and rectifying subtle classification errors in a class of Li\'enard systems. For Hopf bifurcations, extending prior work on necessary conditions [SIAM J. Numer. Anal. 34 (1997)] and sufficient conditions [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 182 (1994); J. Symbolic Comput. 30 (2000)], we establish a complete algebraic characterization via two equivalent formulations: one using Hurwitz determinants and subresultant sequences, and another derived from the greatest common divisor (GCD) of the real and imaginary parts of the characteristic polynomial. From the GCD formulation, we obtain a novel and, for the first time, complete semi-algebraic description of the transversality condition, yielding a decision procedure via triangular decomposition of semi-algebraic systems and heuristic real quantifier elimination. Our approach resolves cases beyond the reach of state-of-the-art polynomial-based methods, and experimental results confirm the feasibility and efficiency of our frameworks.
item.dc:creator: Changbo Chen, Bo Huang, Valery Romanovski, Linpeng Wang

item.title: On the invertibility of saddle-point matrices: exact algebraic conditions and applications to constrained dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.31244v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The solvability of constrained dynamical systems governed by D'Alembert--Lagrange mechanics relies directly on the invertibility of the coefficient matrix describing the underlying saddle-point structure, which couples system inertia with kinematic constraints. Standard formulations often rely on overly restrictive sufficient assumptions, such as global positive definiteness or semi-definiteness of the mass matrix, frequently combined with generalized inverses to handle singular mass distributions. In this work, we establish the purely necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for matrix invertibility: the kinematic independence of the constraints and a kernel intersection condition between the allowed directions of motion and the induced inertial forces. We provide a physical interpretation of this requirement, demonstrating that it eliminates non-zero admissible motions whose generated inertial forces are entirely absorbed by constraint reactions. Furthermore, by completely avoiding generalized inverses, this formulation offers a unified and coordinate-free framework capable of handling massless components and indefinite inertia structures within a computationally robust setting.
item.dc:creator: Federico Talamucci

item.title: Smale's Mean Values And Geometric Mean Values
item.description: arXiv:2611.31546v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, for every integer $d>2$ and every $L>0$, there exists a polynomial of degree $d$ whose geometric mean value exceeds $L$. This result demonstrates that the geometric mean value alone is insufficient to establish the smallest upper bound for the minimum of Smale's mean values. Under certain additional assumptions, we derive upper bounds for the geometric mean value, thereby verifying Smale's mean value conjecture for several subclasses of polynomials. Furthermore, we connect Smale's mean values to Fekete points. Motivated by this connection, we formulate a new problem concerning Fekete points in the spirit of Smale's mean values.
item.dc:creator: Yunping Jiang, Zhe Wang

item.title: Strong convergence rate for non-autonomous slow-fast SDEs driven by Brownian motions and {\alpha}-stable processes
item.description:
arXiv:2611.32058v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish a quantitative strong averaging principle for a class of time quasi-periodic slow-fast stochastic differential equations driven by both Brownian motions and multiplicative $\alpha$-stable L'evy processes. We show that the slow component converges strongly to an autonomous averaged equation with rate $\varepsilon^{\min\{1-1/\alpha_2,\,1/(
u+2)\}}$, where $\alpha_2\in(1,2)$ is the fast stability index and $
u$ comes from the quasi-periodic structure. Our strategy is as follows. We first derive the intermediate step of the averaging principle to average out the effect of fast-variable oscillations on the system, although the averaged variable still depends on $\varepsilon$. We obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1-1/\alpha_2}$. Furthermore, under the uniformly quasi-periodic conditions, we show that the slow component converges strongly to the solution of some autonomous averaged equation, whose coefficients independent of $\varepsilon$. We thus obtain the convergence rate $\varepsilon^{1/(
u+2)}$. The main contribution of this paper is to extend the additive L'evy noise to multiplicative L'evy noise and extend the fast equation of the system from the autonomous setting to the non-autonomous setting. In particular, we establish an explicit convergence rate in the quasi-periodic setting, extending the corresponding results for the periodic case.
item.dc:creator: Xifeng Su, Tianxiang Wang

item.title: Quasiperiodicity breakdown and homoclinic bifurcations in the forced librations of a parametric oscillator
item.description: arXiv:2611.32278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Above its instability threshold, a parametrically excited oscillator settles into one of two phase states. The response of these states to a second, much slower modulation of the same stiffness is investigated. In the rotating frame, this modulation periodically varies the detuning and drives the phase librations. When the modulation is slow compared with the libration frequency, the phase states follow adiabatically. As the two frequencies become comparable, this approximation breaks down and the driven libration resonates with the intrinsic one. This nonadiabatic regime is examined for a Duffing oscillator with nonlinear damping. The averaged equations describe a periodically perturbed planar system with integrable unperturbed dynamics, whose homoclinic loop is derived in closed form. The phase states persist as invariant tori supporting quasiperiodic motion. Their stability and period-doubling bifurcations are captured by a damped Mathieu equation, in which the modulation contributes to both parametric stiffness and parametric damping. A Melnikov analysis yields explicit thresholds for separatrix splitting and the onset of homoclinic intersections, which are corroborated by numerical computations of the invariant manifolds. Numerically it is revealed that these intersections arise well before sustained chaotic motion develops. The fate of the parametric oscillation depends markedly on the resonance condition: modulation at the libration frequency destroys the invariant tori and quenches the oscillation, whereas modulation at twice the libration frequency leaves it intact.
item.dc:creator: Pierpaolo Belardinelli

item.title: Patterson-Sullivan Theory for Approximate Groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.32836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we consider the limit set of a uniformly discrete approximate subgroup acting on a negatively curved manifold, and prove several properties comparable to that of the classical case of discrete groups, including a version of the dichotomy between elementary and non-elementary groups. Furthermore, we adapt the Patterson-Sullivan construction for discrete groups to obtain asymptotic counting results for the orbits of infinite uniformly discrete approximate groups acting on a negatively curved manifold.
item.dc:creator: Isaac Weaver

item.title: A Mathematical Characterization of Neural Activation Induced by Temporal Interference Stimulation
item.description: arXiv:2605.16761v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Temporal Interference Stimulation (TIS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique in which two high-frequency sinusoidal currents with slightly different frequencies generate a low-frequency envelope that can activate deep neural structures. This study investigates the conditions under which TIS elicits action potentials in a single neuron modeled by the FitzHugh-Nagumo system. This research integrates phase-plane analysis and geometric singular perturbation to develop a mathematical framework for analyzing TIS. By combining a mathematical analysis of differential equations with computer simulations, the study elucidates how the amplitudes and beat frequency jointly determine whether the neuron remains quiescent, exhibits only transient responses, or undergoes persistent (tonic) firing.
item.dc:creator: Esteban Paduro, Antoine Chaillet, Mario Sigalotti

item.title: Graph-Induced Rotational Twisted States in Systems of Identical Oscillators
item.description: arXiv:2607.11833v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we study a new class of collective motion for identical coupled Stuart-Landau oscillators on graphs. This model was previously known to converge to the synchronized state for a certain class of initial data. Here, we show that when the interaction matrix is circulant, there exists another class of attractors, in which the particles are uniformly distributed on a circle, reminiscent of the \textit{twisted states} known for the Kuramoto model, but which rotate around the origin. However, contrary to the classical Kuramoto case, here the rotation is caused by the asymmetry of the graph structure, and not by the natural frequencies. We identify conditions for the existence and local stability of the \textit{rotational twisted states}, both in the Stuart-Landau model and in the Kuramoto model. We also provide sufficient conditions for the existence and stability of the synchronized state, which can co-exist with the rotational twisted state in a certain parameter region. We provide a generalization of the class of interaction matrices able to generate rotational twisted states via leader-follower interaction matrices. We show that heterogeneous rotational twisted states can also exist for a system of heterogeneous oscillators, attracted to different individual target amplitudes. This study is accompanied by numerical simulations that illustrate the possible behaviors of the system, which also include metastable dynamics and a chimera state.
item.dc:creator: Nastassia Pouradier Duteil, David Poyato, David N. Reynolds

item.title: Quantitative Gibbs Transfer in Fiber-Contracting Extensions:\ Thermodynamic Formalism, Liv\v{s}ic Theory, and Sharp Logarithmic Distortion
item.description: arXiv:2608.21352v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the transfer of Gibbs estimates between a compact dynamical system and a factor with uniformly contracting fibers. A cohomological identity relates the orbit sums; the remaining issue is the comparison of Bowen-ball masses. Subexponential comparison errors give directional weak Gibbs transfer, while bounded errors preserve strong estimates. We also establish a blockwise sequential version along prescribed Gibbs-time sequences, with errors measured against the full block length. Geometric and conditional-mass hypotheses provide practical criteria for these comparisons. A stationary renewal model shows that the distinction between bounded and subexponential comparison is essential. Its invariant lift to a contracting Cantor-fiber extension is not supported on a measurable graph, and the optimal uniform forward logarithmic error is $\log n+O(1)$. This remains true under fixed changes of the base radius. The reverse comparison, along a specified section, has bounded error. We also give an example in which pointwise subexponential bounds cannot be made uniform. For context, projection gives an affine bijection of invariant probability measures and preserves entropy. When the potentials are cohomologous, invariant averages and pressure agree, as do minimizing measures and equilibrium states in the finite-pressure regime. For H\"older potentials, a continuous section yields a stable-direction reduction, with H\"older regularity under additional assumptions. Subactions and Liv\v{s}ic solutions can then be lifted whenever the corresponding quotient hypotheses hold.
item.dc:creator: Giovane Ferreira

item.title: When vector abundance constrains vector-borne transmission: inside epidemic dynamics within a prescribed population
item.description: arXiv:2610.25971v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The global burden of vector-borne diseases continues to rise, presenting escalating challenges to public health and agricultural systems. Their expanding geographic range and associated impacts underscore the need for tools to project disease dynamics and evaluate interventions. Mechanistic compartmental host--vector models provide such a framework by explicitly representing transmission processes. However, while these models often couple vector population dynamics with infection spread, the inherent complexity of vector demographic processes calls for a more modular approach. In this study, we consider the setting in which the total vector abundance is an externally-prescribed input to a general vector-mediated transmission model. Our objectives are threefold: (i) to provide theoretical guarantees for ensuring consistency between the prescribed total vector abundance and the dynamics of the model compartments, (ii) to characterize model properties related to the local reproduction index (informing extinction or emergence near the time of introduction) and the inter-seasonal propagation, and (iii) to derive insights for diseases transmitted by Aedes albopictus in mainland France. We apply this framework by feeding the epidemiological model with vector-abundance data obtained either from entomological surveillance systems or from an external detailed population dynamic model. Moreover, epidemiological national surveillance data are used to estimate the transmission parameter. Based on this, we derive conditions for emergence and extinction, and show how the extent of the epidemic depends on introduction timing, transmission rate, and susceptible population density. Taken together, these results highlight the value of generating and leveraging entomological surveillance data as well as their model-based counterparts when observations are unavailable (which is particularly relevant in the context of global warming and for the evaluation of vector-control strategies). Overall, we establish a refined framework integrating such data or forecast into compartmental models, with strong potential for a wide range of applications in animal, human or plant health.
item.dc:creator: Lise Isnel (BioSP), Julien Papa{\"i}x (BioSP), Olivier Bonnefon (BioSP), Samuel Soubeyrand (BioSP), Lionel Roques (BioSP)

item.title: Ergodicity of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.27697v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the geodesic flow of a closed, connected surface of negative Euler characteristic with a $C^{3+\mathrm{Lip}}$ metric of nonpositive curvature is ergodic with respect to Liouville measure. The singular set, consisting of directions whose geodesics remain in zero curvature for all time, has zero Liouville measure. Ergodicity then follows from Pesin's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Federico Rodriguez Hertz, Jana Rodriguez Hertz, Weisheng Wu

item.title: Polynomial complexity, random graphs, and strict ergodicity
item.description: arXiv:2611.08973v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct infinite words $w$ whose complexity functions are quadratically bounded, but whose discrete derivatives are not linearly bounded, resolving a question of Cassaigne. Moreover, we construct infinite words of polynomially bounded complexity, and subshifts of quasi-linear complexity, whose discrete derivatives do not decay compared to their complexity functions, thus exhibiting a typical exponentially-growing behavior. As an application, we give the first examples of subshifts of polynomial complexity whose Rauzy graphs do not have Benjamini-Schramm limits. Finally, we realize (up to an inevitable linear error factor) every function satisfying the necessary conditions, as the complexity function of a minimal, uniquely ergodic, cube-free subshift, strengthening previous realization results in this direction, and derive consequences for the growth of simple algebras and just-infinite semigroups satisfying nontrivial laws.
item.dc:creator: Be'eri Greenfeld, Paul-Henry Leemann, Carlos Gustavo Moreira, Efim Zelmanov

item.title: Suppression of gel formation by spontaneous fragmentation
item.description: arXiv:2611.09537v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work we study the discrete Smoluchowski equation with a multiplicative kernel and an additional term describing the spontaneous shattering of each particle into monomers at a constant rate $\lambda$. We show that the introduction of fragmentation suppresses gelation for $\lambda \ge 4$. We derive analytical expressions for the second moment and the monomer concentration $n_1(t)$. These expressions lead to a recurrence relation allowing the steady-state particle size distribution for $\lambda \ge 4$ to be calculated with machine precision. We validate our analytical and semi-analytical results via numerical simulations using a solver that employs the Fast Fourier Transform for computation of the right-hand side and a second-order Runge-Kutta method with adaptive time steps.
item.dc:creator: Sergey Matveev

item.title: Lower semicontinuity of dimension for ergodic and quasi-Bernoulli measures under conformal projections
item.description: arXiv:2611.18752v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how the Hausdorff dimension of a projected symbolic measure varies under perturbations of a conformal iterated function system on the real line. For every fixed shift-invariant ergodic measure, we prove that both its projection entropy and the Hausdorff dimension of its projection are lower semicontinuous in the $C^1$ topology on the defining systems. The proof expresses projection entropy as a supremum of lower bounds obtained from the conditional entropies of finite symbolic partitions. For quasi-Bernoulli measures, we also prove joint lower semicontinuity of the projected Hausdorff dimension when the systems converge in $C^{1+\theta}$ and the symbolic measures converge weakly with a common quasi-Bernoulli constant. These measures need not be shift-invariant. In particular, for Gibbs measures, the dimension is jointly lower semicontinuous in the system and the potential when the potentials vary in a fixed H\"older space $C^\alpha$. No separation assumption is required. Finally, for each fixed shift-invariant quasi-Bernoulli measure, we obtain a dense $G_\delta$ set of systems among those with derivative moduli strictly less than $1/2$ for which the projected dimension equals the minimum of one and the ratio of entropy to Lyapunov exponent.
item.dc:creator: Attila Losonczi

item.title: Reconstructing hidden attractors with reservoir computing
item.description: arXiv:2611.22918v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Hidden attractors are difficult to locate as their basins of attraction do not intersect with any small neighborhood of an equilibrium point. We examine the possibility of reconstructing the hidden chaotic attractor from time series via reservoir computing, where the reservoir is built by a network of driven Kuramoto oscillators. We compare all-to-all coupling, nearest-neighbour ring coupling, and a ring with one modified oscillator equation which ensures that any attractor will be hidden. The numerical results suggest that ring coupling supports accurate reconstruction over a wider range of coupling and forcing strengths than all-to-all coupling. Searches near reservoir equilibria nevertheless show why agreement in short-term prediction and long-term statistics does not establish preservation of hiddenness. Numerics for the modified ring show that it has the highest performance which coincides with our intuition that reconstructing the global dynamics would yield a more faithful attractor reconstruction. We also show that this construction precludes global forgetting of initial conditions for constant inputs, although local conditional contraction along a nonconstant signal remains possible. The distinction between reconstructing attractor dynamics and preserving basin structure provides a basis for evaluating and designing reservoir models of hidden attractors.
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Zaman, Emel Khan, Thomas Geert de Jong

item.title: Rotational Chaos in the Driven Pendulum
item.description: arXiv:2611.29608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Building on recent developments in the topological theory of surface dynamics, we develop readily applicable criteria for computer-assisted proofs of the existence of rotational horseshoes and apply them to the Driven Pendulum. These tools also allow us to localize the resulting instability region, and to compute a lower bound for the length of their rotation sets. This, in turn, implies the existence of periodic points realizing a wide range of rational rotation numbers. The obtained results correspond to physically meaningful parameter values of the Driven Pendulum. The method also applies to periodically forced Hamiltonian systems whenever the stated conditions are satisfied.
item.dc:creator: Maciej J. Capi\'nski, Sof\'ia Llavayol, Alejandro Passeggi

item.title: A smooth compactification of similarity classes of triangles
item.description: arXiv:2408.07792v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a smooth algebraic compactification of the space of labeled, oriented similarity classes of triangles, as a quotient of a 3-point configuration space in the plane -- minus triple-collisions -- by the similarity group. The configuration space is naturally isomorphic to the Fulton-MacPherson space of \cite{FM94} and to the Schubert-Semple space of \cite{Semple}. The quotient is topologically a connected sum of three projective planes, and projects via blow-down to two shape spaces that have appeared in the literature: the well-known 2-sphere (\cite{Kend84}, \cite{Beh}, \cite{Montgomery}, \cite{ES15}), and the less-well-known 2-torus (\cite{BG23}). A natural action by the dihedral group $D_6$ yields a quotient stack describing absolute (unlabeled, unoriented) triangle classes.
item.dc:creator: Eric Brussel, Madeleine Goertz, Elijah Guptill, Kelly Lyle

item.title: The Subtractive Divisor Orbit: Unconditional Bounds, Parity Constraints, and a Conditional Framework
item.description: arXiv:2604.25446v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $a(n)$ be the number of iterations of $F(m)=m-\tau(m)$ needed to reach zero, where $\tau(m)$ counts the positive divisors of $m$. Write $\Delta(n)=a(n)-a(n-1)$. We prove that for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $X$, each of the inequalities $\Delta(n)\ge X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ and $\Delta(n)\le -X^{1/2-\varepsilon}$ holds for at least $X^{1-\varepsilon}$ integers $1\le n\le X$. The proof uses the identity $F(2m)=2F(m)$ at odd $m$ and the fact that an odd orbit first changes parity at a square. For every fixed $C>0$, a positive proportion of starting values $n\in(X,4X]$ satisfy $\left|a(n)-\frac{Cn}{\log n}\right|\gg_C\frac{\sqrt X}{\log X}$. For the hitting time itself we prove $a(x)\ll_b\frac{x}{(\log x)^b}$ for every $b<\log 2$, together with a lower bound having logarithmic exponent $2.988206\ldots$. On complete crossings of $(N,2N]$, with $Z=2N$, the logarithm of the step size has normal order $(\log 2)\log\log Z$, uniformly in the starting value. Computations through $10^9$ give the largest positive and negative first differences in this range.
item.dc:creator: Marco Mantovanelli

item.title: LLM-ACES: Closed-Loop Discovery of Dynamical Systems with LLM-Guided Adaptive Search
item.description: arXiv:2606.25039v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recovering governing ordinary differential equations (ODEs) from data is a central challenge in modeling dynamical systems across scientific domains. Existing approaches cast discovery as a static inference problem over fixed datasets, assuming that the observed trajectories are sufficiently informative. However, dynamical systems evolve over large state spaces, and limited data can make multiple equations observationally indistinguishable, leading to identifiability gaps and the recovery of incorrect governing equations. To address this, we introduce LLM-ACES, or LLM-guided Active Closed-loop Equation Search, a closed-loop framework that jointly optimizes symbolic hypothesis construction and adaptive data acquisition. In LLM-ACES, a large language model (LLM) proposes operator priors that define constrained subspaces of the symbolic search space, within which candidate equations are fit to the observed data. The disagreement among these candidates guides the acquisition of informative trajectories, creating a feedback loop that iteratively refines both the hypothesis space and the discovered dynamics. On 122 ODE systems spanning ODEBench and ODEBase, LLM-ACES achieves the lowest median NMSE, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines while reaching the highest symbolic accuracy up to 70.8% on ODEBench and 69.5% on ODEBase across different LLM backbones. Our analysis further shows that LLM-ACES is sample-efficient, achieving better performance with less data. Under observation noise and sparse sampling, LLM-ACES keeps the lowest reconstruction error without inflating expression complexity, whereas baselines tend to add spurious terms that fit the data locally but obscure the governing relationships. Code: https://github.com/scientific-discovery/LLM-ACES
item.dc:creator: Nikhil Abhyankar, Sha Li, Sanchit Kabra, Naren Ramakrishnan, Yulia Gel, Chandan K. Reddy

item.title: Nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.28597v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce nonnuclear Bunce-Deddens algebras, defined as reduced crossed product C*-algebras associated with free odometer actions of nonamenable countable discrete residually finite groups on a Cantor space. These are nonnuclear counterparts to the generalised Bunce-Deddens algebras introduced by Orfanos. For large classes of groups, we show that they share many regularity properties, including real rank zero, stable rank one, strict comparison of positive elements, and admitting a unique tracial state. In many cases, we deduce that they are even selfless and hence pure. Finally, we compute the ordered K-theory and trace pairing of Bunce-Deddens algebras over nonabelian free groups.
item.dc:creator: Jamie Bell

item.title: Free abelian group actions on projective fibered varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.25778v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional normal projective variety of Kodaira dimension $\kappa$ and $G$ an abelian subgroup of automorphisms such that all elements of $G\backslash \{\mathrm{id}\}$ are of positive entropy. Dinh and Sibony showed that $G$ is actually free abelian of rank $\le n-\kappa-1$. In this paper, we show that after replacing $G$ by a finite-index subgroup, there exists a G-Equivariant Minimal Model Program for the pair $(X, G)$ when $\mathrm{rank}(G)=n-\kappa-1$ and $\kappa>0$, and the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a $Q$-abelian variety provided that the termination of flips holds in this setting.
item.dc:creator: Sichen Li

item.title: Coexistence and extinction in stochastic Lotka--Volterra systems with Volterra--Lyapunov stable interactions
item.description: arXiv:2610.28174v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider stochastic Lotka-Volterra systems $dX=\mathrm{Diag}(X)(\alpha+AX)dt+\mathrm{Diag}(X)\Gamma\,dB$ with nondegenerate noise and a Volterra-Lyapunov stable interaction matrix $A$, that is, $DA+A^\top D\prec0$ for some positive diagonal matrix $D$. This class covers every self-limited predator-prey food web that is conservative in the sense of Volterra, in particular every such web whose interaction graph is a forest. Let $\beta=\alpha-\frac12\mathrm{diag}(\Gamma\Gamma^\top)$ be the vector of noise-corrected growth rates and $m=-A^{-1}\beta$. We show that the process has a stationary distribution under which all species have positive densities if and only if $m>0$. In that case the process is strongly stochastically persistent, and its stationary distribution is unique and has mean $m$. When $m>0$ fails, the species that survive are those present in the unique saturated nonnegative equilibrium $\bar x$ of the deterministic system $\dot x=\mathrm{Diag}(x)(\beta+Ax)$. Almost surely, the occupation measures converge to the stationary distribution of this subcommunity, and $\log X_i(t)/t$ converges to $(\beta+A\bar x)_i\le0$ for every species $i$. The proofs rely on the theory of invasion rates of Hening and Nguyen. For Lotka-Volterra systems, invasion rates are affine in the mean of the underlying measure. Combined with two quadratic identities, this provides explicit weights $Dm$ for their persistence theorem and identifies the limiting regime when persistence fails, without enumerating the invariant measures on the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Ramirez Osorio

item.title: On a conjecture of Velani
item.description: arXiv:2610.28839v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the approximation of elements of the middle-third Cantor set by dyadic rationals, and natural extensions. We prove a conjecture of Velani, completing the metric theory for the Cantor measure. Our key method enables a quantitative study of the incommensurability of binary and ternary expansions of integers, initiated by Furstenberg. The method has other applications, e.g. $\sum_{k} |\hat{\mu}(2^k)|^\sigma < \infty$ for any $\sigma > 0$, where $\mu$ is the Cantor measure.
item.dc:creator: Sam Chow, Han Yu

item.title: Diagonal and fine tower dimensions for minimal circle homeomorphisms and product actions
item.description: arXiv:2611.19895v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.
item.dc:creator: Kang Li, Geng Wang

item.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.22703v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider one-dimensional discrete Schr\"odinger operators with a periodic background and independent Bernoulli disorder. We ask for the least background period permitting infinitely many gaps in the almost sure spectrum. We provide explicit rational parameters at the minimum period of three, answering Wood's question. Our example gives negative answers to Bellissard's question for a disconnected background hull and to Damanik and Fillman's two finite-gap questions for transitive subshifts of finite type and subshifts of positive entropy. The proof, which appears to be new, normalizes the first background value to zero and establishes a transverse heteroclinic connection at nonzero energy. A strict scale window yields invariant multicones. For every nondegenerate Bernoulli law, gaps accumulate from the right at this spectral point. This accumulation persists under small perturbations, with its energy varying real analytically. Spectral intervals approach this point from the right, ruling out a Cantor spectrum. Three is the least background period at which exact recovery of the spectrum from periodic realizations can require unbounded fundamental periods of the total potential.
item.dc:creator: Cong Chen, Yong Li
